newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says Russian sugar tax discriminatory.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says Russian sugar tax discriminatory.

text.p: Ukrainian officials on Wednesday criticised as discriminatory a Russian plan to levy a 10 percent tax on Ukrainian sugar imports and said it would have a disastrous effect on the former Soviet republic's sugar industry.

"Russia's decision is pure discrimination. I would even call it a tragedy. But this is caused by our short-sightedness and inability to foresee developments," Olexander Bohatarenyk, deputy head of the state-run sugar concern Ukrtsukor, told Reuters.
"The only way out is to sit down with our Russian partners and find common ground on this. Ukraine will find no markets other than Russia."
Traders, though, said the tax, to take effect from October 1, would prompt them to find new markets.
One told Reuters it would make it difficult to unload sugar in Russia. "But there are markets in Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Kazakhstan," he said.
"There is a great market in Central Asia," added a second trader.
He said Ukrainian exporters would have to absorb the tax.
"The Russian rules will have a serious effect on the Ukrainian sugar business," he said. "Ukrainian sugar exporters will have to lower their prices by 10 percent."

Russia is imposing the value-added tax on all raw and refined sugar imports from Ukraine to halt dumping of cheap Ukrainian sugar imports, a state customs committee official in Moscow said earlier on Wednesday.
Bohatarenyk said the relatively low quality of Ukrainian sugar made exports to regions other than Russia unlikely.
"I have serious doubts that Ukrainian sugar can compete on markets other than Russia and the CIS. The biggest historical market for Ukraine has been Russia," he said.
Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma said last week that Moscow's proposal to tax Ukrainian imports could spark a protectionist trade war.
Ukraine is expecting to produce a low 2.8 to three million tonnes of refined sugar this year, down from last year's 3.485 million tonnes.
Government officials have forecast exports of no more than one million tonnes of refined sugar from the 1996 harvest.
Most of Ukraine's 1.4 million tonnes of sugar exports in the first half of this year went to Russia.

A Russian government commission recommended last month that all white sugar imports to Russia for 1996 and 1997 be capped at 1.5 million tonnes per year, including one million tonnes from Ukraine, but no decision has yet been taken.
